finding: PR #2041 registers `metal-universe-heavy-metal` as a non-collapsing setKey (parent `metal-universe`); until it merges and deploys, normalizeSetKey collapses that key to `metal-universe`, so the 1996 Fleer Metal Universe "Heavy Metal" 10-card named insert never minted its own card_catalog rows. #2041 PR comments (2026-09-11) measured all ten Heavy Metal numbers against prod card_catalog and found the absorption hits FIVE numbers, 18 rows total: #1 Albert Belle (3 rows), #2 Barry Bonds (6 rows), #6 Mike Piazza (5 rows), #8 Frank Thomas (2 rows), #10 Matt Williams (2 rows). #3, #4, #5, #7, #9 are clean. By source: 17 baseballcardpedia-graded + 1 ingest-auto-seed. Re-measured by this repair 2026-09-12 by point-read: identical 18-row population, identical single sale (on hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe:2:ssp:no-auto, visible only on hobbyiqCardId — byCardId=0, byHobbyiqCardId=1, byEither=1).
rulings: THE 5 BASE-CARD PARENTS AT THESE ADDRESSES ARE CORRECT AND ARE NOT IN THIS FILE. Point-read 2026-09-12 of all 5 plain (`:base:no-auto`, no grade tier) rows at 1996 metal-universe #1/#2/#6/#8/#10: every one is the CHECKLIST-BACKED base player (Roberto Alomar, Brady Anderson, Mike Mussina, Rafael Palmeiro, B.J. Surhoff respectively; source `baseballcardpedia-ladders-2026-09-02`, the checklist authority). These are real, correctly-named base cards and must never move or be touched by this repair. No entry in this file names one of these five plain parent ids as its `id` or its `to`.

CORRECTED 2026-09-12: THE 17 GRADED CHILDREN ARE ENTRIES, NOT EXCLUSIONS. An earlier draft of this file left the 17 graded children out on the theory that "a graded child follows its parent" when a card moves. That rule applies when the PARENT is the row being moved — it is not this shape. Here the parent (the base #N card: Alomar, Anderson, Mussina, Palmeiro, Surhoff) is CORRECT and STAYS PUT; the graded child itself carries the Heavy Metal player's name (a Bonds PSA-9 row sitting under Brady Anderson's card, for example). That is not the child following a moving parent — it is a MIS-PARENTED graded row, and it does real pricing damage: the graded-to-raw rung prices Anderson's raw pool from Bonds's graded sale. Leaving it in place would leave that damage in place. Verified against the real moveCatalogRow 2026-09-12 (in-memory fake container, real prod code from dist/): a graded child CAN reslug to another graded address across a setKey change — both the id and the destination carry a gradeTier, buildIncoming's guard only refuses when gradeTier presence DISAGREES between the two sides (a graded child landing on a plain CARD address, or the reverse). The refusal named in #2041's comment ("a graded child cannot move onto a card address", the 53-failure mode on REPORT run 34356734615) was for exactly that mismatched shape — a graded child aimed at a destination WITHOUT the grade suffix. None of the 17 entries here do that: every `to` carries the same grade tier as its `id`. The move was confirmed to land cleanly and to auto-derive the correct new parentSlug under the Heavy Metal address.

ALL 18 ROWS RESLUG TO THE SAME PLAYER'S ADDRESS UNDER THE HEAVY METAL KEY. The one ungraded row (`...:2:ssp:no-auto`) moves to the Heavy Metal SSP address. Each of the 17 graded children moves to the matching GRADED address under the Heavy Metal key — e.g. `hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe:2:base:no-auto:psa-9` (Barry Bonds, mis-parented under Brady Anderson's card) reslugs to `hiq:baseball:1996:metal-universe-heavy-metal:2:base:no-auto:psa-9`. Every entry's `reason`/`evidence` names both the WRONG parent it currently sits under and the Heavy Metal player/checklist row it belongs to.

keepSales: true. Exactly one sale rests on any of the 18 rows — on the ungraded SSP row, visible only on `hobbyiqCardId` (byCardId=0, byHobbyiqCardId=1, byEither=1, the same field disagreement #2041 flagged for the Finest pool repoint list). None of the 17 graded children carry a sale (measured 2026-09-12: byCardId=0, byHobbyiqCardId=0, byEither=0 on every one). Per CF-A-DISENTANGLEMENT-DOES-NOT-CARRY-THE-OTHER-CARD'S-SALES this reslug separates the Heavy Metal identity from the base-set address it was wrongly filed under; the one sale is a genuine Heavy Metal Bonds sale and belongs at the new address once it exists, but this list does not carry it there itself — the rematch re-derives hobbyiqCardId/cardId against the genuine identity post-ingest.

APPLY ONLY AFTER #2041 SHIPS AND THE HEAVY METAL CHECKLIST INGESTS — CORRECTED FROM 'REFUSED/OCCUPIED'. None of the 18 destinations in this file exist yet: normalizeSetKey still collapses `metal-universe-heavy-metal` to `metal-universe` on the INGEST path until #2041 merges and deploys, and the parent Heavy Metal card_catalog rows are only minted once the Heavy Metal checklist ingest runs (10 rows, per #2041's comment). A REPORT run against the ungraded entry was measured 2026-09-12 and does NOT show refused/occupied as originally expected: normalizeSetKey's collapse only applies at ingest time, not to this lane's literal point-read of the destination slug, and no row exists there to refuse onto — moveCatalogRow's rowAt finds nothing and the report predicts a clean RESLUG. THAT IS THE HAZARD, NOT A SAFETY NET: an APPLY run today would silently mint orphaned, un-normalized rows before the key exists and before the Heavy Metal checklist reconciles against them — worse than a refusal, because nothing stops the write. The gate is therefore a PROCESS gate, not a mechanical one: this file must not be run with BACKFILL_APPLY=true until #2041 is merged, deployed, and the 10-row Heavy Metal checklist ingest has landed at metal-universe-heavy-metal:1 through :10. This file is committed now, per #2041's follow-up comment's instruction to whoever writes the post-ingest fold list, so the list exists and is reviewed before it is needed — but the report's own numbers are not the enforcement mechanism here; the human process gate is.
